title: Flow of local sensitivity in a spin chain coupled to a bosonic bath
abstract: We study how local sensitivity to an encoded parameter, captured by the quantum Fisher information, flows between a spin chain, a coupled bosonic bath, and their quantum correlations, where we treat the bath as a full many-body quantum system beyond the Lindbladian approximation. We analyze how the coupling symmetry determines the destination of the departed sensitivity directly at the level of the Hamiltonian. We consider an excitation-exchanging Jaynes--Cummings coupling, which preserves the total number of excitations, and a spin-excitation-conserving Holstein coupling. We find that the Holstein coupling leaves the bath with no first-order information about the phase and stores the lost sensitivity entirely in spin--bath correlations, whereas the Jaynes--Cummings coupling passes this sensitivity to the bath, in full for a single excitation. The bath spectrum then governs whether the sensitivity ever returns to the spins. It revives fully and periodically when the coupled-system frequencies share a common period, but when those frequencies disperse the departed share dephases across the bath modes and never returns. We note that a transported metrological register loses more sensitivity than its arrival fidelity implies.
summary: This work analyzes the flow of local quantum sensitivity (QFI) between a spin chain and a bosonic bath under different coupling mechanisms. By treating the environment unitarily, it distinguishes between couplings that store lost information in correlations versus those that transfer it entirely to the bath. The findings reveal fundamental dependencies on system periodicity for any potential revival of the initial sensitivity.
main_problem: The study investigates how local quantum sensitivity, quantified by Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), flows between a spin chain and an attached bosonic bath.
main_result: The coupling symmetry dictates the fate of lost information: Holstein coupling stores it in correlations, while Jaynes-Cummings coupling transfers it fully to the bath. Revival depends critically on shared periodicity among system frequencies.
method: The analysis uses a full unitary evolution approach (avoiding Lindblad approximations) to track QFI flow and calculates the 'correlation deficit' ($\Delta F_{sb}$) as a diagnostic tool.
model_or_system: The model consists of a spin chain coupled to a bosonic bath, governed by Hamiltonians including XX exchange, Jaynes-Cummings (JC), or Holstein couplings. The system is analyzed for its unitary evolution dynamics.
key_observables: Local QFIs ($F_s, F_b, F_{sb}$), the correlation deficit ($\Delta F_{sb}$), and time-dependent transfer functions $ ar{F}_s(t)$.
important_parameters: Coupling type (JC vs. Holstein), bath spectrum/frequencies, and resonance conditions ($t_B = J/2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis treats the bath as a full many-body quantum system undergoing unitary evolution; some results rely on approximations like superselection rules or single-excitation sectors.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate JC exchange dynamics showing QFI oscillation (resonance vs. off-resonance) and confirm tensor network convergence for both coupling types.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares the flow of sensitivity under different couplings, analyzing local block diagnostics ($\Delta F_{sb}$) against site-summed quantities to diagnose coherence transfer efficiency over time.
why_interesting: It provides a detailed quantum information perspective on open system dynamics, showing how entanglement and correlation storage govern metrological resource decay in realistic physical models like spin chains coupled to baths.

A spin chain with uniform or engineered exchange coupling (blue lines) couples to a local bosonic mode per site (red levels, featuring a local frequency and nearest-neighbor hopping). A parameter phase is encoded on a localized block of sites (blue dashed rectangle) and read out at later times from another restricted region of sites (orange dashed rectangle).

FIG. 2. Jaynes–Cummings exchange at resonance on the uni- form XX chain [exact single-particle solution, L = 40, ω0 = 0, tB = 0.5J, λ = 0.5J, edge encoding]. (a),(b) Spin and bath QFI densities Fs(j, t) and Fb(j, t). By Eq. (12) these equal the occupations exactly, and the block deficit vanishes iden- tically. (c) Site-summed shares (dashed: closed-form result).

FIG. 3. Jaynes–Cummings off resonance [L = 40, ω0 = 2J, tB = 0.3J, λ = 0.5J; exact single-particle solution, edge en- coding]. (a) Single-qubit QFI density Fs(j, t); the occupation maps coincide with the QFI densities, as in Fig. 2, and are omitted. (b) Site-summed shares (dashed: closed-form re- sult): the site-summed share ¯F s collapses to a plateau as the channels dephase, while the deficit ∆¯F sb remains zero.
